title: Started as a quick prototype to test Opus 5.5 and Sol 6.1, now I’m turning it into a full cyberpunk × Japanese folklore action game
author: the_builder_ai
selftext:
I’ve been experimenting with building games using AI, trying out different styles and genres. 

I landed on this 2.5D cyberpunk side-scroller set in a neon Japanese city filled with spirits and yokai, and enjoyed working on it so much that I’ve decided to develop it into a full game. I also wanted the city to feel like somewhere you’d explore, with a strong atmosphere and music along with quieter moments such as festival stalls, karaoke, and mini-games between the fights.

Still a work in progress, but I’d love some honest first impressions.

What do you care about most in a game like this? Does the visual style work for you? From the footage, does the combat look satisfying or feel like it needs more impact?

Any feedback would be appreciated!

I’ll also be sharing devlogs and updates on X if you’d like to follow along [@thepaulymarket](https://x.com/thepaulymarket)

comments.author: titanunveiled
comments.body: The background art work looks great!!! Any tips on getting opus to do what you want? For me it’s like pulling teeth

replies.author: the_builder_ai
replies.body: Yes - anything or areas in particular you would like to know about? In general, I use Sol/Astra to generate the artwork and then Opus does most of the coding and putting them together. I have Opus log every change in every version and areas of do's and dont's so it remembers
